hook: A 1950 letter from Mexican 'Ideographic Inventor' Miguel Angel Garcia Macias to a U.S. scientific commission proposes that flying saucers are atomic-powered stratospheric aerostats of U.S. manufacture, accompanied by a translated Mexican newspaper account claiming the first photograph of a flying saucer was taken over Durango at 9,000 feet by engineering student German Horacio Robles Jr.
why_it_matters: This document illustrates the FBI's practice of collecting unsolicited international civilian correspondence and foreign press clippings as part of its early UAP case file, capturing how the 1947–1950 flying saucer wave was perceived abroad — specifically, the assumption that the objects were secret American atomic technology. The Durango photograph claim, if the newspaper clipping is authentic, represents an early documented instance of photographic evidence submitted to U.S. authorities from a non-U.S. source. The inventor's detailed pseudoscientific propulsion proposals, submitted in good faith, show how the U.S. government was a magnet for public UAP speculation even from foreign nationals with no apparent official connection.

key_findings.finding: A Mexican civilian inventor wrote directly to the U.S. government asserting that flying saucers are atomic-powered aerostats already possessed by the United States, framing the disclosure as a civic duty.

quotes.text: This deals with stratospheric aerostats (?)* or Flying** saucers as people commonly call them, and which I believe your great Nation, making use of ATOMIC force, possesses.

I hope that my idea is Studied and approved by the said Commission and may serve for the Progress of the Universe instead of its DESTRUCTION, and for the good of all of us human beings who inhabit the Earth.

key_findings.finding: Garcia Macias proposed a 'Global-Conic' stability theory for the craft, claiming they could exceed the speed of light or sound depending on atomic material quantity, and could be launched from ground or water.

quotes.text: These apparatuses can be used in order to avoid Atomic Explosion on the Earth, since the velocity is Greater than that of Light or Sound in accordance with the quantity of Atomic Material which is used in their fabrication. These apparatuses can be thrown from the ground or from
the Water since the Conic-Global or Global-Conic form permits it.

key_findings.finding: A Mexican newspaper account (translated for the FBI file) claimed engineering student German Horacio Robles Jr. photographed a flying saucer over Durango at 8,000–9,000 feet and described the object as a double truncated cone moving via jet propulsion.

quotes.text: THE FIRST PHOTOGRAPHS OF A "FLYING SAUCER", OBTAINED IN DURANGO AT AN ALTITUDE OF 9000 FEET

The apparatus seems to be a double truncated cone, joined at its bases which moves by something like jet propulsion and which displaces itself by changing position in order to use its motive force in the direction desired, for which reason it can be seen under apparently different forms.

key_findings.finding: The newspaper account identifies Robles Jr. as a student at the National School of Engineering and notes he sketched the craft's real form and handed over photographs to an editorial office, suggesting the images were submitted to a Mexican publication before reaching the FBI.

quotes.text: Mr. German Horacio)Robles Jr., student at the National School of Engineering, is one of the thgusands of persons who have seen "with their own eyes" the flying saucers or disks which have become the general topic of commentaries and have given rise to the most varied hypotheses.

The future civil engineer, porenig eyes Jr. sketched in our editorial offices after having reported his obser ions on the flying disk and after having handed over the pictures of this apparatus which he had obtained.

key_findings.finding: The document includes a technical diagram page with labeled components — Oxygen Chamber, air current directions, propeller, and vacuum levels — consistent with the inventor's pseudoscientific propulsion theory, translated by Mrs. Sophia Saliba.

legacy_program_connections.reasoning: This civilian correspondence and foreign press clipping was collected as part of the FBI's early UAP case file (62-HQ-83894), representing the type of public reporting and unsolicited theory submissions that fed into the broader U.S. government UAP tracking effort of the late 1940s–1950s.

The inventor explicitly theorizes that flying saucers are propelled by nuclear-atomic force, referencing atomic material quantities as determining speed — a civilian echo of AEC-era atomic propulsion research discourse.
